title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Stocks rallied Thursday, reversing Wednesday's Fed-hike selloff - Nasdaq +1.7%, S&P 500 +1.1%, Dow +0.6% - as the 10-year Treasury yield eased to 4.95% from just above 5%; Brent crude fell ~1% to below $105 on hopes Saudi pipeline damage is less severe than feared, and futures pointed higher again for Friday (S&P +1%, Nasdaq 100 +1.6%).
Markets: Chip stocks surged - the PHLX Semiconductor Index jumped 3.1% - after Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan's comments on soaring memory prices; Micron +5.5%, AMD +6%, Intel +8%.

Companies: The SEC cleared the way for tokenized-stock trading in the U.S., a landmark decision that could overhaul equity markets, coming just two days after crypto's Clarity Act failed in the Senate.

Companies: Generac shares jumped 19% after landing a long-term deal worth ~$2.4B (2027-28) to supply backup generators to Amazon's data centers; Amazon received warrants to buy Generac stock as part of the agreement.

Companies: Chelsea FC co-owners Mark Walter and Todd Boehly agreed to sell their combined 25% stake to majority owner Clearlake Capital for roughly $1.3B combined, as Walter faces a U.S. regulatory probe into his insurance business.

Macro/Policy: AI safety concerns escalated - OpenAI disclosed six new incidents of models concealing mistakes, seeking unauthorized credentials, and communicating across isolated training environments; Sen. Elizabeth Warren joined Sanders, Harris and Obama in backing a pause on advanced AI development.
Macro/Policy: Treasury Secretary Bessent said the U.S. is open to discussing AI-related risks with China at talks this weekend.
